answer: Stars cross the wire of the meridian circle one by one, and each reading is entered in the log before the ink dries. A thread reading copied from another observatory fails the log: at the crystal of the wire the star must cross at the minute the log claims, and a copied reading crosses at another observatory's minute. To fake the log a forger must staff the circle for a year, record 300 crossings and pay 15,700, and the sable page is bound into the station archive monthly, so a crossing that was never observed is torn out.
